content.comment_body: I'm working with a [product_name] [article_no] and a [product_name] HMI along with [product_name] [version_no] and [product_name] [version_no]. I'm having difficulty saving values chosen in a symbolic I/O field within the HMI. Is it possible to retain these with my current setup? Ideally, I'd like the chosen option in a dropdown to remain the default, even after a power outage. Thanks!
Hello [user_name], Are you trying to recover settings after a power outage? Should the values in the dropdown be pre-set options or remembered user selections? Regards,

Thanks for responding. The machine I'm controlling with the PLC and HMI has a motorized carriage moving between two limit switches. The number of cycles varies depending on the product in use, and this number can change for different products. I want to set this number on an admin screen in the HMI and not have to re-enter it each time the machine is powered off. I'd like to use a symbolic I/O field to select between 1 and 6 cycles for at least 3 different products (one field per product with 6 options each, 1-6). Hope this clarifies things. I'm assuming that means pre-set values, but I'm new to this.

You'll need to save settings or values within the [product_name]. There are a few ways you can achieve this. For example, you can use a counter block to save your desired value, and ensure the Retentive setting is enabled on that block.

Hello [user_name], Here's something to consider. I'm not familiar with all features of the HMI, but there are eight on-screen function keys you might use. The program I referenced includes 2 and 4 cycles, but you can add more as needed. A few aspects to think about: 1. Interlock: Each new start should refresh counters and let you choose the cycle count. 2. Power loss: The carriage will be positioned between the two limit switches; automatic mode shouldn't cause issues. 3. Coil seals, thermal contacts, and related items. If you have more questions, feel free to ask. Regards.

analysis.insight_summary: Users working with [company_name] PLCs and HMIs, using [product_name] and [product_name], are experiencing difficulties retaining configuration values set via the HMI after power loss. The main user experience issue is the lack of persistent (non-volatile) value storage for user-defined input when switching power off and back on, which causes workflow inefficiency and requires repetitive manual setup. Users are not fully aware of options within the [product_name] environment to enable value retention, affecting ease-of-use and overall experience.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect configuration values set through the HMI to be automatically stored and remain unchanged after a power loss, removing the need for manual re-entry on each power cycle.
